note: Report excellent: 17 findings, correctly separated load-bearing ledgers from drift, auditable clean-file list. Edits rejected: mechanical s/now/should/ demoted three TRUE shipped-state claims (levelMin/levelMax in troop.lua + validator_core.lua + map-editor.js) into pending work, and inverted the encounterSteps gap statement into design intent. Lesson: 'find X' delegates well, 'fix X' needs the delegate to verify each claim against code first -- which the brief did not require.

Measurement task ('find X'), the class the n=1 row predicted would delegate well. It did. Headline finding correct and independently verified: 0 sealed faces is real, because viewport_3d.lua:1335 addFace returns early when the neighbour is a wall, so the resolved face list excludes wall-to-wall adjacency by construction. Remaining win is exterior-only, 916/2518 = 36.38% across 13/13 maps, none skipped. Classifier's sealed branch is genuinely exercised by tests rather than a dead path returning zero, and the opening-adjacency negative control (visually enclosed but must be visible) is the correct control and works. Two defects found in review: ceilingQuads derives #structure.floorCells so it counts walkable cells rather than emitted quads (map_renderable_bundle has three ceiling paths, only one is addQuad); and renderable_bundle.collect() is asserted then discarded, which is both wasted work and the natural fix for the first defect. One false claim: reported a 'pre-existing test_map_geometry_export crash' and refused to claim the unit gate green because of it. The refusal was exactly right discipline; the premise was wrong. A clean main worktree gives ALL UNIT TESTS OK. The crash was filesystem contention from working inside the primary checkout, same root cause as the .git/index.lock permission denial it also hit. Worktree isolation was not followed, but the preamble did not require it at the time - that gap was ours, closed by #298. Lesson: goal mode suits bounded measurement with deterministic verification. Its weak point is environmental attribution - it cannot tell a collision from a pre-existing defect, so any baseline claim it makes needs re-measuring on a clean tree.
